content.title: Natural Street Interaction Mechanism
content.summary: Turn a vertical street conversation into one executable action chain. The characters keep moving as distance, gaze, pace, and gesture change their relationship; environmental parallax, shifting daylight, and live sound prove spatial continuity, and the ending lands on a clearly readable interaction state.

quick_start.input_format: Vertical street setting + two stable identities + reason to interact + continuous walking route + visible relationship change + readable ending
quick_start.recommended_input: A market florist notices a travel photographer walking beside the stall. They exchange two short lines while continuing along the same route; their spacing, gaze, and pace visibly soften before the florist points out a side street and the photographer acknowledges it without stopping.
required_anchors: Immediately establish a reason for interaction at the opening
Camera movement tracks the subject's spatial path
At least one visible change in distance, gait, gaze, or gestures
Ambient parallax, light, shadow and live sound remain continuous
The end is readable rather than abruptly truncated
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: Vertical street interviews, chance encounters, and walk-and-talk scenes driven by one continuous route and a visible relationship change.
Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.
MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 projects that need a reusable causal video structure.
not_suitable_for: Requests that copy the source identity, setting, props, dialogue or shot order.
Concepts that cannot show all required anchors inside the target duration.
Long-form exposition or unrelated multi-location stories without a compact causal chain.

creative_dna.mechanism: A single social premise drives the change in distance between the characters and the camera along the continuous street route; performance, parallax, moving natural light and live sound jointly advance the relationship to a readable end.
applicable_scope: Street interviews, chance encounters, city walks and character introductions
Clothing, Beauty, Travel and Lifestyle Short Films
H3 Ref2VA or Seedance multimodal reference that needs to keep character identity and clothing stable
Interactions that can be articulated by a continuous chain of actions in 4–15 seconds
not_suitable_for: Long-form monologues, complex debates, or ensemble performances spread across multiple locations
Precise choreography, extensive hard cuts, or frame-by-frame recreations of real people and locations
usage_steps: Clarify the purpose, duration, frame, character relationships, route and ending of the interaction
Assign unique and narrow identity, costume, environment, action or voice responsibilities to each input material
First write the causal chain from approach to communication, relationship change, and final beat; then decide whether a cut is necessary.
Trim the dialogue to fit the duration, then compile it with the native syntax required by H3 or Seedance.
Check identity, gait, route, light and shadow, hand contact, sound and time closure
invariants: Immediately establish a reason for interaction at the opening
Camera movement tracks the subject's spatial path
At least one visible change in distance, gait, gaze, or gestures
Ambient parallax, light, shadow and live sound remain continuous
The end is readable rather than abruptly truncated
quality_repairs: All events must fall within the actual target duration
For a 10-second clip, prefer two or three short lines; remove lines before increasing speaking speed
Don’t start the second shot at the end of the film
Prefer verbal or gestural positioning. Any physical contact must be explicit, consensual, and physically plausible.
Don’t replace motion, light, shadow, and spatial design with fictional 4K tags
anti_copy_exclusions: Do not copy the appearance, clothing, or body styling of the sample characters
Do not copy the composition and dialogue of the original tree-shaded streets and fenced roads
Change at least six of character type, relationship, location, route, costume, dialogue, shot realization, and ending simultaneously

review.method: canonical-source offline English editorial pass with terminology and stable-token validation; title naming editorial pass
